title: [roundtrip-sweep] `ModelMessagesTypeAdapter`: `RetryPromptPart.content` list of error details fails to round-trip when any item lacks `input`
author: github-actions[bot]

comments.author: pydanty[bot]
comments.body:
<!-- pydanty:status-comment:v1 -->

**pydanty: pr-ready** — localized bug in message-history (de)serialization.

**Classification:** bug.

**Why this matters:** Anyone whose message history contains a RetryPromptPart with a structured `content` list missing required TypedDict keys loses the ability to round-trip through `Agent.all_messages_json()`, `new_messages_json()`, or durable-execution replay. Once serialized, the JSON becomes unloadable, causing data loss or workflow paralysis. A simple fix at the RetryPromptPart type boundary reduces that state-loss risk and removes the PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue noise for the framework's own `error.errors(include_url=False, include_context=False)` output.

**Evidence summary:** Maintainer history shows this class of round-trip failure is fixed narrowly at the message-type boundary (Issue #5696 / PRs #5697, #5698: add missing part to the discriminated union). It also shows RetryPromptPart error-dict key omission is deliberate policy: PR #4947 (approved by DouweM) strips `input`/`ctx` from retry content, then PR #5181 (DouweM) narrowed this to NativeOutput retries while preserving `input` for tool-call retries. The current reader (`ErrorDetails` TypedDict) is incompatible with the writer's chosen omissions, making round-trip a one-way door. Reproduction in the issue body demonstrates `ModelMessagesTypeAdapter.validate_json(serialized)` raises `ValidationError: input field required`. The code boundary is `pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/messages.py` (`RetryPromptPart.content`, `error_details_ta`, and `model_response()`).

**Playground share URL:** No share could be created in this run; the reproducer delegate could not reach the local checkout and the issue body already contains the failing test and traceback.

**Next action:** PR-ready. Reason: this is a reproduced, localized bug with a clear boundary in messages.py; maintainer history supports narrow round-trip fixes at that boundary and shows the key omissions are intentional. No API-design discussion is needed.

comments.author: urbantech
comments.body:
One low-risk acceptance bar that seems worth preserving here: `dump_json -> validate_json` should succeed for every shape the runtime already emits today, not just the canonical `ErrorDetails` shape.

Concretely, I would add regression coverage for at least three payload families:

1. tool/native retry content missing `input`
2. framework-generated content missing `ctx` / `url`
3. the same payload after JSON round-trip has normalized `loc` as a list instead of a tuple

That would keep the fix tied to the real contract boundary: persisted message history must remain reloadable across replay / restart / version bump, even when the error-detail dict is only partial.

Implementation-wise, loosening the serialized boundary is probably safer than trying to re-tighten every writer. If maintainers still want a richer in-memory shape, a normalize-on-read step feels less risky than requiring every historical payload to satisfy the full `TypedDict`.
